checks: Finitely many integer fibers are disjoint in the ambient space and isometric to the continuous sections. The largest dimension q gives positive finite total intrinsic mass; lower-dimensional sections have zero q-measure.

At a positive anchored combination, the direction space of the Minkowski average is the sum of input directions. Since its actual integer target has dimension at most q, each q-dimensional input and the output share this direction. The reasoning is local to the participating incidence and does not assume a common direction across the whole contact set.

In that common intrinsic direction space, the ordinary Brunn–Minkowski lower bound and affine-majorant upper bound coincide at the actual target. Positivity places the target in E, and equal-volume containment of the two compact q-bodies implies exact equality. The strict-separation/interior-ball argument establishes the needed strictness of volume under proper containment.

For q≥2 the positive-volume two-body equality case gives positive homothety. Grouping and the equality of both successive bounds justify the many-body induction. For q=1 the intervals are already homothetic. The centroid identity follows from a common homothetic representation and does not invoke unrestricted additivity of centroids.

Representing each point of the centroid hull over an integer base by its positive coefficients proves it is exactly the actual centroid at a base in E. This gives lattice completeness, the singleton integer sections and same-parity midpoint closure.

The weighted graph selection keeps the actual unequal weights a_z and produces one mark before testing any cap. A containing cap with nonconstant fiber restriction uses the full-volume centroid estimate in the intrinsic q-plane. A constant containing restriction includes all that fiber, including a whole fiber on the boundary.

Summation retains at least gamma_q times captured centroid weight, hence gamma_q W_E/2^n. The derivative log(t/(t+1))+1/(t+1) is negative, so q≤d gives gamma_q≥gamma_d. The proof covers rank zero directly and the empty E branch has a zero bound at any feasible point.

For a nonconstant affine majorant the positive contact roots and volumes can differ, so the prior theorem does not give their centroid graph.
